subject: Rubicon demo: intermittent websocket EOFs + chunked-transfer drops (urgent)
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex+infra@rubicon.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live demo — stream drops and 503 bursts

Hi Stephanie,

Quick heads-up from this morning's demo with our ops team: during a 20-min load run (roughly 40 concurrent user sessions) they saw repeated short-lived socket EOFs and chunked-transfer closures — roughly every ~30–90 seconds a stream would abruptly end with no final token. The UI shows an indefinite spinner (no trailing error), and we also see client-side retries that spike request volume which then results in a cluster of 503s from your edge for 45–60s shortly after.

I attached a small capture from our side and the timings. We can reproduce this reliably against the streaming websocket endpoint: wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream. We're in a tight timeline — this behavior blocks our planned rollout next week.

Can you confirm whether this is a network/proxy cut or something on the inference side?

Thanks,
Alex Park
Platform Engineer, Rubicon Health
[Attachment: rubicon-capture-20270419.pcap (pcap, 4.1MB)]

Subject: Re: Live demo — stream drops and 503 bursts

Thanks Alex — and sorry you're running into this during the demo. We saw traces that line up with the timestamps you provided; sending this to infra + runtime so we can triage.

Immediate asks:
- Can you send a short example request payload you used (prompt + headers) and confirm whether you were using streaming over WebSocket or chunked HTTP?
- If you can reproduce, please keep one session open and share the exact UTC timestamp for the next occurrence so we can correlate server logs.

Planned next steps from our side: Dev will pull edge logs and proxy metrics; Rishi will look at the runtime's KV-cache / handler timeouts for the same window. If we see client retries producing a burst of requests, we may suggest a temporary mitigation: enable non-streaming sync fallback for some routes and a short client-side exponential backoff to avoid the retry spiral.

I'll keep you posted within the hour.

—Stephanie

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Alex Park <alex+infra@rubicon.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live demo — stream drops and 503 bursts

Alex / team — quick triage from edge: we see spikes in 502/503 from our HTTP gateway at 09:04:23–09:05:12 and again at 09:16:37–09:17:25 UTC. During those windows the edge process reported a surge of connection resets originating from a small set of client IPs (likely retrying clients).

Initial observations:
- Proxy timeouts: some chunked HTTP connections are getting reset when backend inference takes >8s to return the first token; gateway has a default keepalive/idle-config at 10s.
- WebSocket: we observed abrupt ``EOF`` with no CLOSE frame; upstream reported connection reset (RST) at TCP layer.
- Throughput pattern: sustained token-per-second load ramped 2.5x at 09:15 which correlates to the second burst.

Attachments: I've uploaded a trimmed set of wire-level logs and the proxy metrics snapshot for 08:58–09:30 UTC.

Immediate mitigation we recommend:
1) On your client side, switch streaming session to a short-lived sync call for critical flows (we can provide an SDK toggle).
2) Enable client exponential backoff with jitter to avoid tight retry loops.
3) We'll temporarily widen the gateway idle timeout to 22s and add a short server-side buffer for first-token latency.

I'll open a support ticket and push a config change to canary within the hour.

- Dev
[Attachment: wirelogs-20270419.txt (text/plain, 1.2MB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Park <alex+infra@rubicon.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live demo — stream drops and 503 bursts

Thanks Dev — dug into the runtime traces. Two noteworthy findings:

1) KV-cache thrash: for a subset of requests (model variant x-llama-small-q), cache miss paths are taking ~120–180ms extra per invocation due to an LRU promotion race under high concurrency. That alone doesn't explain abrupt EOFs but contributes to first-token latency.
2) Backpressure handling: when the runtime is under sustained token pressure and the network layer sees repeated TCP resets, token flushing to the socket can race with stream teardown which results in partial-chunk drops. Our gRPC-to-websocket translator currently doesn't re-send partial frames once the socket is gone.

Actionables I've pushed to canary:
- Increase soft-timeout for first-token emission to 18s on canary; add a flush-on-close hook to attempt graceful terminal chunk emission (best-effort) before tearing connection.
- Enable a lightweight per-session token-window to limit extreme tail latencies causing client retries.

These are rolling to canary now; we should have telemetry within ~30 minutes. If we confirm improvement we'll push to prod and coordinate maintenance window with Rubicon ops.

- Rishi
[Attachment: heap-snapshot-20270419.bin (binary, 48MB) referenced for internal triage]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex+infra@rubicon.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, ops_lead@rubicon.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 17:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live demo — stream drops and 503 bursts (warroom + next steps)

Alex / team — quick update and next steps after the canary run:

What we did:
- Deployed canary changes: gateway idle tuned to 22s, runtime first-token soft-timeout bumped to 18s, flush-on-close best-effort enabled, and a token-window backpressure guard.
- Asked Rubicon to hold a controlled replay of the 40-session load for 15 minutes.

What we saw:
- Partial-chunk occurrences dropped by ~85% in the canary telemetry window; client-visible EOF rate fell from 0.9% -> 0.14%.
- 503/502 bursts reduced significantly when client retries were rate-limited by backoff.

Immediate actions for rollout:
1) We recommend rolling the canary changes to 10% of traffic in your prod region for the next 24 hours while monitoring token-delivery success and gateway errors.
2) Rubicon to enable client-level backoff (we provided our SDK snippet) and switch critical flows to sync endpoints for the next 72 hours as a safe fallback.
3) We'll follow up with a postmortem including logs and perf diffs; Grace will coordinate a short executive summary for your leadership.

Can we schedule a 30-minute warroom at 09:00 PDT tomorrow to approve the 10% rollout and confirm monitoring dashboards?

Thanks for the quick collaboration — appreciate the detailed capture which made correlation fast.

—Stephanie
